Daily Turkmen › 1,000 words

The first 100 Turkmen words of the deck

The first 100 words of the Daily Turkmen deck, the most common ones, each with its meaning in English, an example sentence and, for verbs, the main forms (he, she or it). 99 of them are taught in the lessons of the course.

Learn them with spaced repetition, Anki-style: open the flashcards. Free, no account needed.

Overview1–100101–200201–300301–400401–500501–600601–700701–800801–900901–1000
  1. 1
    birnumber

    one; a, an

    Bir käse çaý beriň.

    A bowl of tea, please.

    As a, an it comes before the noun: bir kitap (a book). Turkmen has no word for the.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 2: Vowel harmony and plurals

  2. 2
    bolmakverb

    to be; to become; to happen

    Näme boldy?

    What happened?

    present bolýar · past boldy · general present bolar · converb bolup

    On its own, Bolýar means OK. In tenses where "to be" needs a verb, it is bolmak: Ertir öýde bolaryn (I'll be at home tomorrow).

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 1: The past tense· Conjugation of bolmak

  3. 3
    -myparticle

    question particle (yes-no questions)

    Sen talypmy?

    Are you a student?

    Written attached to the word it questions: gelýärsiňmi?, dälmi? -my after back vowels, -mi after front vowels.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 4: Questions and negation

  4. 4
    bupronoun

    this; this one

    Bu näme?

    What is this?

    Its case forms start with m: muny (this, as an object), muňa (to this), munda (in this). Plural bular (these).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 2: Vowel harmony and plurals

  5. 5
    menpronoun

    I; me

    Men mugallym.

    I'm a teacher.

    Dative maňa (to me), genitive meniň (my), accusative meni (me). Needed with the future in -jak, which has no personal ending: Men geljek.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 1: Letters and sounds

  6. 6
    senpronoun

    you (one person, familiar)

    Men gowy, sen nähili?

    I'm fine, how are you?

    Dative saňa, genitive seniň (your). Use siz with strangers and older people.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 3: Saying who you are

  7. 7
    olpronoun

    he, she, it; that

    Ol meniň dostum.

    He's my friend.

    No gender: ol is he, she or it. Dative oňa, genitive onuň, accusative ony. Before a noun, that: ol jaý (that building).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 2: Vowel harmony and plurals

  8. 8
    nämepronoun

    what

    Seniň adyň näme?

    What's your name?

    Näme üçin? (why?).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 1: Letters and sounds

  9. 9
    hemconjunction

    also, too; and

    Men hem gelýärin.

    I'm coming too.

    After a pronoun it is often contracted: menem (me too), senem. Hem … hem means both … and.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 4: Questions and negation

  10. 10
    weconjunction

    and

    Aýna we Merdan mekdepde.

    Aýna and Merdan are at school.

    Hem-de (and also) joins longer phrases.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 4: Questions and negation

  11. 11
    etmekverb

    to do; to make (in compound verbs)

    Sen näme edýärsiň?

    What are you doing?

    present edýär · past etdi · general present eder · converb edip

    t becomes d before a vowel and before -ýär: edýär, eder. It builds many compound verbs: kömek etmek (to help), jaň etmek (to call).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 6: The present tense· Conjugation of etmek

  12. 12
    zatnoun

    thing

    Bazardan köp zat aldym.

    I bought lots of things at the market.

    Bir zat (something), hiç zat (nothing), hemme zat (everything).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 2: Vowel harmony and plurals

  13. 13
    üçinpostposition

    for; for the sake of

    Bu sowgat seniň üçin.

    This present is for you.

    Pronouns before it take the genitive: meniň üçin, seniň üçin. Näme üçin? (why?), şonuň üçin (so, that's why).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 12: Requests and company

  14. 14
    islemekverb

    to want; to wish

    Men çaý içmek isleýärin.

    I want to drink tea.

    present isleýär · past isledi · general present islär · converb isläp

    Another verb before it stays in the infinitive: gitmek isleýärin (I want to go).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 6: The present tense· Conjugation of islemek

  15. 15
    baradjective

    there is, there are; present, existing

    Öýde çörek barmy?

    Is there any bread at home?

    With a possessed noun it means to have: Meniň maşynym bar (I have a car). The opposite is ýok.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 5: Where things are

  16. 16
    dälparticle

    not (with nouns, adjectives and the future)

    Bu meniň kitabym däl.

    This isn't my book.

    Negates nouns, adjectives and the future in -jak: talyp däl, geljek däl. Other verb forms take -ma/-me.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 4: Questions and negation

  17. 17
    köpadverb

    a lot, much, many; very much

    Köp sag boluň!

    Thank you very much!

    Nouns after it stay singular: köp adam (many people). Very before an adjective is örän or gaty.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 5: Where things are

  18. 18
    gelmekverb

    to come

    Ol ertir geljek.

    She's coming tomorrow.

    present gelýär · past geldi · general present geler · converb gelip

    Hoş geldiňiz! (Welcome!) is its past tense.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 6: The present tense· Conjugation of gelmek

  19. 19
    bilmekverb

    to know; can (after a verb in -yp)

    Men türkmençe azajyk bilýärin.

    I know a little Turkmen.

    present bilýär · past bildi · general present biler · converb bilip

    After a verb in -yp it means can: Ýüzüp bilýärin (I can swim). Bilmeýärin (I don't know).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 6: The present tense· Conjugation of bilmek

  20. 20
    ýöneconjunction

    but

    Men isleýärin, ýöne wagtym ýok.

    I'd like to, but I don't have time.

    Emma also means but, a little more formal.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 4: Questions and negation

  21. 21
    gitmekverb

    to go; to leave

    Ertir Mara gidýärin.

    I'm going to Mary tomorrow.

    present gidýär · past gitdi · general present gider · converb gidip

    t becomes d before a vowel and before -ýär: gidýär, gider, gidip. For going to a place, barmak is also common.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 6: The present tense· Conjugation of gitmek

  22. 22
    hawainterjection

    yes

    Hawa, men türkmen.

    Yes, I'm Turkmen.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 1: Letters and sounds

  23. 23
    gowyadjective

    good; well; fine

    Ýagdaýlaryň nähili? – Gowy, sag bol.

    How are you? – Fine, thanks.

    Also an adverb: gowy gürleýär (speaks well). Gowy görmek means to like.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 1: Letters and sounds

  24. 24
    aýtmakverb

    to say; to tell

    Maňa adyňy aýt.

    Tell me your name.

    present aýdýar · past aýtdy · general present aýdar · converb aýdyp

    t becomes d before a vowel and before -ýar: aýdýar, aýdar. Aýdym aýtmak (to sing).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 12: Requests and company· Conjugation of aýtmak

  25. 25
    bu ýerdeadverb

    here

    Bu ýerde kim ýaşaýar?

    Who lives here?

    Literally in this place. Also şu ýerde (right here); bu ýere (to here), bu ýerden (from here).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 5: Where things are

  26. 26
    almakverb

    to take; to buy; to get

    Bazardan çörek aldym.

    I bought bread at the market.

    present alýar · past aldy · general present alar · converb alyp

    Satyn almak says to buy more precisely. Alyp gelmek (to bring).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 8: Definite objects· Conjugation of almak

  27. 27
    ýokadjective

    there is no, there isn't; no; absent

    Öýde hiç kim ýok.

    There's nobody at home.

    Also the everyday no: Ýok, sag bol (No, thanks). With a possessed noun, not to have: Wagtym ýok (I have no time).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 1: Letters and sounds

  28. 28
    bermekverb

    to give

    Maňa suw beriň.

    Please give me some water.

    present berýär · past berdi · general present berer · converb berip

    The polite imperative beriň with a dative is a common way to ask for something.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 8: Definite objects· Conjugation of bermek

  29. 29
    diýmekverb

    to say; to mean; to call (by a name)

    Ol näme diýdi?

    What did he say?

    present diýýär · past diýdi · general present diýer · converb diýip

    Bu näme diýmek? (What does this mean?). Diýip introduces quotes and reasons.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 7: Converbs I: after, before, without, until· Conjugation of diýmek

  30. 30
    hasadverb

    more; even more

    Bu kitap has gyzykly.

    This book is more interesting.

    Makes comparatives: has uly (bigger). The thing compared takes -dan: Batyr Myratdan has uzyn (Batyr is taller than Myrat).

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 8: Comparing

  31. 31
    seretmekverb

    to look; to watch

    Maňa seret!

    Look at me!

    present seredýär · past seretdi · general present sereder · converb seredip

    Takes the dative: maňa seret. t becomes d before a vowel and before -ýär.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 7: To and from· Conjugation of seretmek

  32. 32
    görmekverb

    to see

    Men ony düýn gördüm.

    I saw him yesterday.

    present görýär · past gördi · general present görer · converb görüp

    Gowy görmek (to like). After a verb in -yp, to try: Okap gör (try reading it).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 8: Definite objects· Conjugation of görmek

  33. 33
    wagtnoun

    time

    Wagtyň barmy?

    Do you have time?

    Şu wagt (right now).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 9: My family

  34. 34
    çenlipostposition

    until; up to, as far as

    Agşama çenli işleýärin.

    I work until the evening.

    Takes the dative: agşama çenli, Aşgabada çenli. -dan … -a çenli is from … to.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 7: To and from

  35. 35
    ýalypostposition

    like, as

    Ol ejesi ýaly owadan.

    She's beautiful like her mother.

    Comes after its noun: ejesi ýaly (like her mother).

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 8: Comparing

  36. 36
    bizpronoun

    we; us

    Biz Aşgabatda ýaşaýarys.

    We live in Ashgabat.

    Dative bize, genitive biziň (our).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 3: Saying who you are

  37. 37
    bolýarinterjection

    OK, all right; it's fine

    Ertir gel. – Bolýar!

    Come tomorrow. – OK!

    The present tense of bolmak, used as OK. Bolýarmy? asks Is that OK?

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 1: Letters and sounds

  38. 38
    işnoun

    work; job; business, matter

    Işim köp.

    I have a lot of work.

    Işe gitmek (to go to work), işde (at work). Işlemek (to work) is built on it.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 7: To and from

  39. 39
    sizpronoun

    you (plural); you (polite)

    Siz nireli?

    Where are you from?

    The plural you, and the polite you for one person. Dative size, genitive siziň (your).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 3: Saying who you are

  40. 40
    herdeterminer

    every, each

    Her gün çaý içýärin.

    I drink tea every day.

    Her gün (every day), her hili (all kinds of).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 6: The present tense

  41. 41
    biripronoun

    someone, somebody; one (of them)

    Gapyda biri bar.

    There's someone at the door.

    Olaryň biri (one of them).

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 5: Can and can't

  42. 42
    näme üçinadverb

    why

    Näme üçin gelmediň?

    Why didn't you come?

    Literally for what. The answer often starts with sebäbi (because).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 4: Questions and negation

  43. 43
    türkmennoun

    Turkmen; a Turkmen (person)

    Men türkmen, Aşgabatdan.

    I'm Turkmen, from Ashgabat.

    Written in lowercase, as an adjective and a noun: türkmen dili (the Turkmen language), türkmençe (in Turkmen). The country is Türkmenistan.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 3: Saying who you are

  44. 44
    nähiliadverb

    how; what kind of, what … like

    Howa nähili?

    What's the weather like?

    Ýagdaýlaryň nähili? (How are you?).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 1: Letters and sounds

  45. 45
    nädipadverb

    how, in what way

    Bazara nädip barmaly?

    How do I get to the market?

    Asks how something is done; nähili asks what something is like.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 10: Passive and reflexive

  46. 46
    özpronoun

    own; oneself, -self

    Bu meniň öz öýüm.

    This is my own house.

    With possessive endings it means -self: özüm (myself), özüň (yourself), özi (himself, herself).

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 10: Passive and reflexive

  47. 47
    ýa-daconjunction

    or

    Çaý ýa-da kofe?

    Tea or coffee?

    Always written with a hyphen.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 12: Requests and company

  48. 48
    şupronoun

    this (here); this one

    Şu kitaby al.

    Take this book.

    Points closer than bu, or at what was just mentioned. Accusative şuny.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 2: Vowel harmony and plurals

  49. 49
    şolpronoun

    that (very); the same

    Şol gün men öýde däldim.

    That day I wasn't at home.

    Points back to something already known: şol adam (that man, the one we talked about).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 2: Vowel harmony and plurals

  50. 50
    galmakverb

    to stay, to remain; to be left

    Şu gün öýde galýaryn.

    I'm staying at home today.

    present galýar · past galdy · general present galar · converb galyp

    Gijä galmak (to be late).

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 3: The future· Conjugation of galmak

  51. 51
    diňeadverb

    only, just

    Maňa diňe suw gerek.

    I only need water.

    şeýleadverb

    so, like that; such

    Men hem şeýle pikir edýärin.

    I think so too.

    Şeýle-de bolsa (even so).

  53. 53
    adamnoun

    person, human being; man

    Bazarda köp adam bar.

    There are many people at the market.

    After numbers and köp the noun stays singular: köp adam. Adamlar (people).

    pikir etmekverb

    to think

    Men seniň hakda pikir edýärin.

    I'm thinking about you.

    present pikir edýär · past pikir etdi · general present pikir eder · converb pikir edip

    Pikir is a thought or an opinion. Öýtmek also means to think, in the sense of to suppose.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 12: Reported speech· Conjugation of pikir etmek

    soňadverb

    later, then; after (with -dan)

    Işden soň öýe gidýärin.

    With -dan it means after: nahardan soň (after the meal).

    tapmakverb

About this list

These are the 1,000 words of the Daily Turkmen flashcard deck, in the deck's order: roughly how common each word is. The ranks are an editorial estimate, not a count from a Turkmen corpus. Words are listed in their dictionary form (verbs in the infinitive, gelmek; nouns in the nominative singular).

The order is adapted from the deck of Daily Turkish, the sister course, which is itself adapted from the 2018 Turkish list of FrequencyWords by Hermit Dave, made from the OpenSubtitles2018 corpus: each word was matched by meaning to its usual Turkmen equivalent, then the list was edited by hand. The order is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0. The meanings, example sentences and notes are original to Daily Turkmen.
